decision.summary: The inspection found no urgent issues, but noted a dog flap and some marks on a Bedroom 1 wall. The landlord says the flap was not approved and asks about a spare key after a lock change. I replied to the landlord, asked the tenant the open questions, added a note, set a follow-up for 23 Feb and returned the job to auto mode.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: The inspection is complete, with no defects beyond the command-strip marks. It is outstanding on the dog flap approval, the lock change and spare key, and the landlord name mismatch.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Questions to the tenant by email (REQ-102) and a reply to the landlord by email (MSG-101). Review on 23 Feb.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not yet. A human is needed only if the flap consent or the lock change turns into a dispute about the tenancy, deposit or legal matters.

args.body: Thanks for your email. The inspection report (16 Feb) records that a dog flap has been fitted in the back door and utility room. Our records don't show any approval for it, and nothing about a lock change. We are asking the tenant who fitted the flap and whether they had permission, and who changed the front door lock, when, and for a spare key to be given to us. We'll update you by 23 Feb. Please can you confirm whether you did approve the flap or not? Also, our records name the landlord contact as Oliver Bennett but your email was signed Felix Clarke. Please confirm who we should deal with. Nothing has been decided about the flap yet, and we are not acting on the tenant's deposit or tenancy.
